title: AI, Machine Learning & LLM Systems
tagline: Statistical foundations, deep learning with PyTorch, Transformer architectures, and production RAG pipelines
description: From linear algebra and scikit-learn models to deep learning with PyTorch, Transformer self-attention mechanisms, LLM application architecture, vector databases, and fine-tuning.
prerequisites: Foundations of linear algebra and probability

stages.title: Stage 1: Mathematical Foundations & Data Stack
stages.description: Matrix operations with NumPy, data wrangling with Pandas, linear regression, and classification metrics.

nodes.title: Linear Algebra, Vector Embeddings & NumPy
nodes.description: Matrix multiplications, dot products, eigenvalues, cosine similarity between high-dimensional vectors, and vectorized operations.
nodes.whyItMatters: Modern AI models represent text, audio, and images as high-dimensional vectors. Measuring semantic similarity relies on vector dot products and cosine distance.
keyTakeaways: Vector embeddings convert discrete symbols into continuous coordinate spaces where semantic meaning equals geometric proximity.
Avoid Python for-loops over arrays; utilize vectorized NumPy operations computed in C-level SIMD instructions.
Understand precision and recall tradeoffs using ROC-AUC and F1-score rather than raw accuracy on imbalanced datasets.
nodes.interviewTips: Be prepared to explain cosine similarity vs Euclidean distance and compute matrix dimension compatibility for matrix dot products.

stages.title: Stage 2: Deep Learning & Transformers
stages.description: Neural network backpropagation, gradient descent, PyTorch tensors, and self-attention mechanisms.

nodes.title: Transformer Architecture & Self-Attention
nodes.description: Query, Key, Value (Q, K, V) scaled dot-product attention, multi-head attention, positional encodings, and encoder-decoder vs decoder-only (GPT) architectures.
nodes.whyItMatters: Transformers revolutionized natural language processing and computer vision, forming the foundation of every modern Large Language Model (GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, LLaMA).

resources.title: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al.)
Andrej Karpathy: Let's build GPT from scratch

keyTakeaways: Self-attention calculates attention weights: softmax((Q * K^T) / sqrt(d_k)) * V, enabling parallel token processing across the entire context window.
Positional encodings inject token sequence order information since self-attention is permutation-invariant.
Modern LLMs use decoder-only architectures trained to predict the next token via causal language modeling.
nodes.interviewTips: Interviewers will ask you to explain why dividing by `sqrt(d_k)` is necessary in scaled dot-product attention (to prevent vanishing gradients in softmax).

stages.title: Stage 3: Production LLM Systems & RAG
stages.description: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), chunking strategies, vector search (HNSW), prompt engineering, and evaluation.

nodes.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Architecture
nodes.description: Augmenting LLMs with private proprietary context: document parsing, semantic chunking, vector embedding generation, vector database indexing, and re-ranking.
nodes.whyItMatters: LLMs hallucinate and lack private organizational knowledge. RAG grounds responses in verified enterprise data without requiring expensive model retraining.
keyTakeaways: Optimal chunking (typically 500-1000 tokens with 10% overlap) preserves context while keeping embeddings focused.
Use hybrid search combining dense vector semantic retrieval with sparse BM25 keyword search for maximum recall.
Apply a cross-encoder re-ranker (Cohere, BGE) on top-50 retrieved passages before sending top-5 to the LLM context window.
nodes.interviewTips: Expect questions on how to prevent hallucinations in RAG pipelines and measure retrieval quality using Ragas metrics (Faithfulness, Answer Relevance).
